name: Creamy Avocado-Basil Pasta with Corn and Tomatoes

ingredients.name: short pasta, such as, fusilli or casarecce
ripe Hass avocados, pitted, peeled, and chopped
kosher salt, plus more to taste
serrano chile, stemmed, seeded, and chopped
finely minced red onion, from 1 small onion

instructions.primary_message: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook pasta until al dente according to the package's instructions. Reserve 1 cup pasta water, then drain. Allow pasta to cool slightly, about 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a blender, combine avocados, crema, lime juice, basil, Parmesan, 3 teaspoons salt, serrano, garlic, and 1/4 cup reserved pasta water. Blend until smooth, adding 2 tablespoons of pasta water at a time as needed to achieve a smooth, creamy consistency, about 1 minute.

Transfer warm pasta to now-empty pot or a large bowl. Add avocado sauce and toss well until pasta is evenly coated, adding additional pasta water 2 tablespoons at a time as needed until sauce is creamy, glossy, and generously coats pasta.
Fold in tomatoes, corn, hearts of palm, if using, and red onion. Taste and adjust with additional salt as needed.
Transfer to a serving bowl. Top with basil and lime zest. Serve.

schema_metadata.keywords: Avocado pasta, creamy pasta, avocado pasta sauce, no-cook pasta sauce, summer pasta recipe

description: This easy summer pasta combines sweet corn and cherry tomatoes with a creamy no-cook avocado-basil sauce that comes together in minutes.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 6 tablespoons fresh lime juice (from 3 to 4 limes), plus finely grated lime zest for serving; 1/2 cup packed basil leaves, plus torn leaves for serving; 8 ounces canned or jarred hearts of palm, sliced into 1/4-inch coins (about 1 1/2 cups), optional

Optional substitutions: crema cream → sour cream

Notes: Sour cream is thicker than crema and may require additional pasta water to achieve a saucy consistency.

Make-ahead and storage: While this pasta is meant to be enjoyed warm, it can also double as a pasta salad when chilled. If served as a cold pasta salad, it is best eaten within 8 hours of being made, before the avocado sauce begins to brown. Do not reheat, as the avocado sauce can separate and lose its bright flavor.
Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days, but the sauce will take on a brown appearance and less fresh flavor as time passes.
author: Laila Ibrahim
